question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?

answer.reasoning: The question asks one thing: how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed (the sources do not say how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed). Law 3.1 sentences (1) and (2) give the test procedure (full underhand stroke, contact over the back boundary line, hit at an upward angle parallel to the side lines), and Law 3.2 sentence (1) gives the pass criterion (landing not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line, per Diagram B). ITTO 3.5.4.4 (1) adds how the Referee assesses the test result (manner of hitting and correct location, per Law 3), which is part of checking the speed. ITTO 3.6.3 (1) (Referee re-checking speed during play) bears on the question without answering the how-to-check part, so it goes in related_sentences. Diagram B contains only the label 'DIAGRAM B' with no citable sentence.
answer.answer: To check whether a shuttle has the right speed, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line [1], and the shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines [2]. A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line [3]. When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit (strength of shot and trajectory), and whether they were hit from the correct location (over the back line) [4].
